use_case_summary: Mid-market SaaS product team building outbound SDR chat agents that can perform CRM/email/calendar actions (tool calling) and stream real-time responses to users. Primary goal: reduce SDR handle time and automate follow-ups while keeping live agent handoff. Need low-latency streaming (<150ms first token target for US region), reliable tool calls (idempotency, retry semantics), and predictable unit economics for 50–75 concurrent agents. Evaluating hosted API first to validate agent UX, then moving to Dedicated for throughput and SLA. Interested in Optimize recommendations for batching, KV caching, and quantization to control costs.
notes:
- Customer: Ironwood builds a mid-market sales acceleration suite — heavy outbound focus.
- Quote from VP Product: "We need the agent to feel instantaneous — streaming latency is user-facing."
- POC scope: 3-week hosted POC; verify streaming performance, tool-call reliability to Salesforce and Gmail API, end-to-end SSO demo.
- Tech asks: support for function/tool calling patterns, per-request routing (region + cost tier), prefix caching to speed repeat interactions.
- Volume profile: peak 50 concurrent agents doing 1–3 messages/second aggregated; average agent session ~12 turns.
- Cost sensitivity: medium — willing to pay for Dedicated if throughput predictable and unit cost beats hosted at scale.
- Compliance: US data residency required for PII, audit logs mandatory for compliance team.
- Follow-ups: SE to run latency benchmark harness (streaming first-token) and provide model variant recommendations for quality/latency trade-offs.
